title: fix: mark text rows that completed with no billable usage
author: davealan74
pr_body_excerpt:
- A 200 whose usage can't be extracted and whose model has no determinable fee fell through to a plain unbilled row — indistinguishable in Tinybird from a legitimately free one.
- Adds `errorTracking` to `ResponseTrackingData`; the `!modelUsage` fallthrough sets `errorResponseCode: "usage_missing"` for `generate.text`, and settlement `emitRow` prefers it over the status-derived data.
- `adjustmentOnlyBilling` keeps first refusal, so models with a knowable flat fee are unaffected. #12212's `perplexity-fast` repro is already covered by that mitigation (it bills the static search fee) — this closes the residual hole where no charge is determinable at all. Nothing on the Portkey side changes.
- Telemetry only: the client still gets its 200. For streams the bytes are on the wire before tracking runs; pre-send empty-stream → 502 is #12921. New row shape for dashboards: `responseStatus` 200 with a populated `error_response_code`.
- Extends `test/tracking-observability.test.ts` (33 pass): non-streaming, streaming, streaming via community endpoint, plus a flat-fee regression guard.
- #13086 rewrites these lines (`notBilled` → `tracked`); needs a rebase depending on merge order.

Addresses #11675

gist.headline: Missing usage gets a flag
gist.blurb: Some successful text responses arrived without extractable usage or a billable fee. They now leave a tiny, useful breadcrumb instead of blending into the free-row meadow.
gist.summary: Text-generation tracking now marks HTTP 200 responses with unextractable usage and no determinable model fee as `error_response_code: "usage_missing"`, while preserving adjustment-only billing for known flat-fee models such as `perplexity-fast`.
gist.impact: Clients still receive the same successful responses, while Tinybird dashboards can distinguish genuinely free calls from successful calls whose billable usage could not be determined.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy observability garden: Polli acts as a careful field inspector, placing a small "USAGE MISSING" marker beside a healthy-looking code plant that has no measurable nectar reading. A nearby CRT monitor robot displays a 200 status and a dashboard row, making the distinction between free flowers and unknown-usage flowers visible.
